_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 41 (Pharaoh's dreams; Joseph rises). Saadia-specific: v.6 'משובה בריח אלקבול' = 'scorched by the qibla wind' (Saadia identifies קדים — east wind — with the qibla-direction wind); v.16 'מן ג'יר עלמי' = 'apart from my knowledge' (Joseph credits God, not himself); v.43 'אלצריף הד'א שריף אלמלך' = 'Behold, this is the king's noble' (Saadia's gloss for אברך — interprets as a herald's cry of noble status); v.45 'מוצ'ח אלכ'פאיא' = 'Revealer of Hidden Things' for צפנת פענח.

translations.1: When two full years had passed, Pharaoh saw — and behold, he was standing on the bank of the Nile.
translations.2: And there came up out of it seven cows — beautiful in appearance and stout of flesh; and they grazed in the reeds.
translations.3: And seven other cows came up after them out of the Nile — ugly in appearance and lean of flesh; and they stood beside them on the bank of the Nile.
translations.4: And the cows of ugly appearance, lean of flesh, ate up the seven cows of beautiful appearance, stout of flesh. And Pharaoh awoke.
translations.5: Then he slept, and saw a second time — behold, seven ears of grain had come up on one stalk, full and good.
translations.6: And behold, seven other ears, thin and scorched by the qibla-wind, sprouted up after them.
translations.7: And the thin ears swallowed the seven full and stout ears. And Pharaoh awoke — and behold, it was a dream.
translations.8: And it was in the morning — his spirit was troubled. And he sent and called for all the learned men of Egypt and all its sages; and he recounted his dream to them — but none could interpret it for him.
translations.9: Then the chief of the cupbearers spoke before him, and said: 'I make mention of my offense today.
translations.10: Pharaoh had been wroth with his servants, and placed me in the custody of the house of the chief of the executioners — me and the chief of the bakers.
translations.11: And we saw a dream on one night, I and he; and the dream of each was according to its interpretation.
translations.12: And there was with us a Hebrew youth, a slave of the chief of the executioners; and we recounted them to him, and he interpreted them for us — interpreting for each according to his dream.
translations.13: And as he interpreted for us, so it was: the king restored me to my office, and impaled the other.'
translations.14: And Pharaoh sent and called for Joseph; and they hurried him from the prison; and he shaved his hair, and changed his garments, and entered to Pharaoh.
translations.15: Pharaoh said to him: 'I have seen a dream, and there is no interpreter of it; and I have heard about you that when you hear a dream, you interpret it.'
translations.16: Joseph answered, and said: 'Apart from my own knowledge — God shall answer Pharaoh with peace.'
translations.17: Then Pharaoh spoke with him, and said: 'I saw — behold, I was standing on the bank of the Nile;
translations.18: and seven cows came up from it, stout of flesh and beautiful in form; and they grazed in the reeds.
translations.19: And behold, seven other cows came up after them — gaunt, exceedingly ugly in form, lean of flesh; I have not seen the like of them in all the land of Egypt in their ugliness.
translations.20: And the lean and ugly cows ate up the seven former stout cows.
translations.21: And they entered into their bellies — but it was not apparent that they had entered; and their appearance was as ugly as at first. Then I awoke.
translations.22: Then I saw — behold, seven ears had sprouted upon one stalk, full and good.
translations.23: And behold, seven ears, withered, thin, scorched by the qibla-wind, sprouted up after them.
translations.24: And the thin ears swallowed the seven good ears. I said this to the learned men, but no one told me anything.'
translations.25: Joseph said to him: 'Pharaoh's dream is one. What God is about to do, He has shown Pharaoh.
translations.26: The seven good cows and the seven good ears — they are seven years of plenty; this is one dream.
translations.27: And the seven lean and ugly cows that came up after them, and the seven empty ears, scorched by the qibla-wind — they shall be seven years of famine.
translations.28: This is the matter which I have spoken to Pharaoh: what God is about to do, He has shown to Pharaoh.
translations.29: There shall come upon you seven years of great plenty in the land of Egypt;
translations.30: then seven years of famine shall come after them; and all the plenty in the land of Egypt shall be forgotten; and the famine shall almost consume the dwellers of the land.
translations.31: And no trace of that plenty shall be apparent in the land, because of the famine that comes after it — for it shall be exceedingly grievous.
translations.32: And as for the repetition of the dream to Pharaoh twice — it is because the matter is established from before God, and He hastens to do it.
translations.33: Now therefore let Pharaoh see a man understanding and wise; let him set him over the land of Egypt.
translations.34: And let him appoint that he set deputies over the land, to collect a fifth of the produce of the land of Egypt in the seven years of plenty.
translations.35: And let them gather all the food of these good years that shall come, and store up their grain under the hand of Pharaoh's deputies, and keep food in their cities.
translations.36: And let it be a deposit therein, for the seven years of famine which shall be in the land of Egypt — and let the dwellers of the land not be cut off by the famine.'
translations.37: And the words were pleasing to Pharaoh, and to all his officers.
translations.38: Then Pharaoh said to his officers: 'Can we find one like this — a man in whom is the spirit of God, knowledge?'
translations.39: Then he said to him: 'Inasmuch as God has made known to you all these things, there is none so understanding and wise as you.
translations.40: You shall be over my house, and according to your order shall all my people be guided; only by the throne shall I be greater than you.'
translations.41: Pharaoh said to him: 'Look — I have set you over all the land of Egypt.'
translations.42: Then Pharaoh removed his signet ring from his hand, and set it upon Joseph's hand; and he clothed him in garments of fine linen, and placed a chain of gold upon his neck.
translations.43: And he made him ride in his chariot-of-state; and they cried out before him: 'The noble — this is the king's noble!' And he set him over all the land of Egypt.
translations.44: Then he said to him: 'I am Pharaoh; and apart from your counsel no man shall lift his hand for a pen, or his foot for a stirrup, in all the land of Egypt.'
translations.45: And he named him Revealer-of-Hidden-Things (Tzafnat-Paaneah); and gave him as wife Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On. And Joseph went out, as governor over all the land of Egypt.
translations.46: And Joseph was a son of thirty years when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. And when he went out from before him, he traveled all the land of Egypt.
translations.47: And the land brought forth, in the seven years of plenty, by the handful — granaries full.
translations.48: And he gathered all the food of these seven years, which had been in the land of Egypt, and placed it in its cities — placing the food of the fields of each city around it, in its midst.
translations.49: And Joseph gathered grain, exceedingly much, like the sand of the sea — until he stopped counting, for it was beyond counting.
translations.50: And to Joseph were born two sons, before the year of famine came — whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
translations.51: And Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh — saying: 'God has caused me to forget all my misery, and all that was from my father's house.'
translations.52: And he named the second Ephraim — saying: 'God has made me grow in the land of my affliction.'
translations.53: Then the seven years of plenty, which had been in the land of Egypt, came to an end.
translations.54: And the seven years of famine began to come, as Joseph had said; and there was famine in all the lands — but in all the land of Egypt there was food.
translations.55: And when the dwellers of the land of Egypt became hungry, the people cried out to Pharaoh for food; and he said to them: 'Go to Joseph; whatever he says to you, do.'
translations.56: And when the famine spread upon the face of all the land, Joseph opened all that was in them, and supplied the Egyptians; and the famine grew strong in all the land of Egypt.
translations.57: And many from the lands came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph; for the famine was severe in their lands.
